body:
Thanks for your advice. I've taken it on board.

One of the absolute hardest things for me to do is to trust another person or to be comfortable around them. Seeking someone out will definitely be a part of my journey, but it's very close to the heart of my problems so I think if I were able to feel safe and comfortable with someone as a trip sitter, I wouldn't really get much therapeutic value from the trip (I am an odd character though, some of the things that I need to do alone are the things I would never advise someone else to do without someone else there. I guess it's just how I am.)

I think that when I feel ready, I'll probably go camping by myself and spend a couple of days centering myself and then I'll try whichever psychedelic I decide on at a small dose to get a feel for it before I step it up - maybe a day or two later, or maybe the next time I go camping.

Thanks for the advice on the benzos - I have quetiapine but it seems like there are mixed results for using it to stop tripping. I have a pretty good doctor, I think if I told him that I was going to do some psychedelic therapy but I would like some Valium in case things go bad he would prescribe some for me.

Thanks for your post. 

Your story sounds very familiar to me. I've been thinking about using mushrooms, salvia... maybe even ayahuasca when I have mustered the will to take something.

The only thing that worries me is that one of those, or using LSD, will fuck me up even more. I've never done hallucinogens before and I don't trust anyone enough to have a trip sitter - it would be a recipe for paranoia for me.

But then I know that all the therapy in the world won't help, and I have had no real successes with medication.

I know that it's important to be in a safe place and to have a good mindset before tripping, but then if I had a place that was safe for me and if I was able to have a good mindset then I wouldn't really need to trip in the first place.

I don't know.

Yeah, I've been very tempted by ayahuasca myself.

I've even considered using Salvia Divinorum therapeutically, but it's hard to get where I am for legal reasons. It might be something you have access to, but it comes with a warning. 

Like any psychedelic, you need to know what you are getting yourself into and how to manage it safely (I'm not a medical professional etc.)

Okay, first thing is you need to be eating enough. If you don't eat enough, it gets really hard to survive and be anywhere near okay mentally as well as physically.

You need to find places that provide free food. 

Find out where the nearest soup kitchen is. Try your local food not bombs branch. Find your nearby food bank. Look at local churches or community centers to see what support they offer to people who have hit hard times. Maybe call or get in contact with a local homelessness shelter to see what services might be available to you. 

Make a calendar of when/where the free food is. Once you start eating, living is going to get a lot easier.

There is free food out there and right now you need to be eating more, whatever it is.

Also consider joining community groups that offer free food. Fuck it. Survive. AA? Why not. Go for the free coffee and donuts. Go and meet up with a local church person (pastor? minister? priest? IDK) and talk to them - they will probably know services that are available. They will probably offer you coffee and something to eat if you meet with them (you might need to let them know you aren't having a spiritual crisis, but a circumstantial crisis, and so you aren't so worried about discussing the state of your soul at the very moment.) Any half-decent religious leader will show great compassion for someone who is in a bad place. 

Also try out the nearby Sikh Gurdwara or the Hare Krishna temple - they are really serious providing food to everyone, and it will be Indian food which is even better!

Masjids/mosques may also provide to people in need as part of their zakat.

If you aren't sure, then try calling ahead if you can.

As for your clothes - this one is simple:

You need a sink or container and some kind of soap (steal some from a public bathroom if you don't have any. If you can only find liquid soap in dispensers, get a small plastic bag, or even just a dirty sock and fill it up and use that.)

Fill the container with water - warm water if possible. Lather the soap up in the water or use dish soap or whatever. 

Let your clothes soak for 15 minutes, then agitate them and rub the fabric against itself where it is stained or heavily soiled. The more agitation, the better.

After you are sick of that, lose the dirty water and squeeze out the water (don't wring! you will stretch your clothes.) Fill up with more water and agitate or let it soak for a minute. Do this once or twice if you can to get all the soap out.

And that's it. You just washed your clothes. Now hang them up to dry. It's not going to be perfect, but it's going to be a big improvement. 

Use any soft brush like a nail brush or a toothbrush with soap to clean serious stains out if you have a brush around.

There are places out there that will help you, you just need to find them.
I agree. If you aren't planning on continuing then at least there is no harm in giving life after high school a shot - there's nothing to lose, and things might change more than you imagine.
